Here is how to scale. 

First thing you need is a winning funnel. Everyone knows that Russell Brunson image — traffic → offer → backend. That’s all it is. A funnel is just your traffic, your offer, and what you sell them on the backend.

Your product is just a solution to a problem that can acquire customers profitably. That’s the easiest way to look at it. You need a big TAM, strong margin, and something unique. TAM just means a million+ people with a common problem. Margin — I look for minimum 3x, ideally 4–5x, because as you scale, CAC goes up. Meta will fluctuate day to day, so you need room for that. Unique can mean a lot of things — delivery, ingredients, speed, or a breakthrough in compliance.

If you don’t have that, and you’re in a commoditized market, you can still win through positioning (being niche-specific), stacking (multi-benefit like “24-in-1”), or authority. I sold hydrogen water bottles that were the same as everyone else’s. The difference? I positioned them as “used by Gary Brecka.” They used that in ads, site copy, even podcasts. That one angle made them print insane numbers.

Now, niche-wise — you can go broad or narrow. I’ve got a free community. That’s technically a product. It’s niche, not massive TAM, but because it’s low competition, high engagement, and a clear path, it still works. Or something like a bed or sauna — smaller TAM, but high ticket, high clarity, can still win.

Margins — if you’ve got 30% margins but strong LTV (like subscriptions), you can make it work. I prefer 50–60%, but early on, don’t get obsessed with it.

Ads. People overcomplicate this. Your ad just needs to interrupt your target audience’s scroll and profitably drive a click. It needs to validate the problem, show your unique mechanism, and drive a profitable KPI.

You need three things: avatar, awareness, and tone. Your ad speaks to one person, one problem, one solution. Match the level of awareness — unaware, problem-aware, solution-aware, product-aware. Don’t sell backpacks to unaware people. Everyone knows what a backpack is. Go for solution-aware: “This backpack fits more, weighs less.” Or problem-aware: “Your backpack is ruining your back — here’s why.”

Your ad has to be native. If you’re running on Meta, people scroll all day. If your ad looks like an ad, you’re cooked. Make it look organic — like content. Use whitelisted pages. Instead of your brand logo, run it under a name like “Stacy White.” Same ad, lower CPMs. If you’ve got multiple creators, make it a family photo profile pic — looks way more natural.

Landing page — keep it simple. Most of your traffic never scrolls past the Buy Now button. Your hero images have to convert. They need to instantly communicate emotion + transformation. You can have the prettiest page ever, and it won’t matter. Simple > pretty. The goal is to align their mindset from ad → page → purchase. Nothing else.

Match awareness. If your ad is problem-aware, don’t send them to an advertorial meant for unaware people. That’s why I like listicles — they work for everything except totally unaware traffic. “5 reasons why [avatar] is loving [product].” It just works.

Offer. Everyone says it, but it’s true — your offer isn’t your price. It’s the whole stack. Product, price, bonuses, guarantees, urgency. A 30-day money-back guarantee is part of your offer. “Try for free, charge after 7 days” — also an offer.

You just need congruency. If you’re selling a water bottle, don’t make your upsell an ebook on Pilates. That happens more than you’d think. Keep everything pointed at the same outcome.

Once that’s dialed, you’ve got a winning funnel. Let’s say it’s doing $1K/day — that’s proof of concept. Next, you scale through creatives.

That’s the whole game. Not SEO, not awareness campaigns — more creatives.

Video ads, image ads, UGC. Analyze what spent and what didn’t. Understand why. The best way is through Google Data Studio — take your ads, plug them in, and it’ll break everything down.

Then improve. Make a checklist: 5 things that worked, 5 that didn’t. Every new batch runs through that checklist. If it doesn’t pass, don’t launch.

Then test. Let it run 2–3 days, then scale what works. Once you find a winner, compound it.

Take that winning ad concept and run it from different perspectives. If your main avatar’s a black woman, run the same concept from her POV. Then from a doctor’s POV. Then from a therapist’s. Same message, new voice.

Add pre-sale pages — congruent listicles and advertorials. If your winning ad goes straight to a PDP, make a listicle that matches the ad’s tone and drive traffic there instead. It’ll rip.

You can scale this infinitely. Change perspective, audience, season, or angle. Same concept, new spin. When I was scaling a brand earlier this year, I took a male-targeted concept, rebuilt it for women, and 3x’d daily revenue that week.

Image ads — cheapest way to scale or retarget. There are two goals: convert missed sales or drive new traffic. Don’t overthink it. Analyze your video ads. Find the biggest emotional pain point. Make static creatives that dramatize it. Make them ugly, make them raw. Dramatic imagery + big red headline = low CPCs.

Your goal is just cheap traffic. Then you convert it with congruent landing pages and listicles. That’s where the real profit comes in.

Once you’ve got a winning advertorial, start split-testing headlines and heroes. Don’t waste time rewriting paragraphs — focus on what they see first.

Then, the big scale — build a team. Hire an image editor in the Philippines. Teach them your style. Have them crank variations nonstop.

UGC — this is how you get infinite creative volume. Seed products to creators through platforms like TikTok Shop or Incense. Offer high commissions. Funnel them into a Discord. Inside that Discord, post winning ads daily, offer prizes, and let creators copy top performers.

When one ad hits, 100 people remake it. That’s how brands like Comfort and NeuroGum are running thousands of ads a day.

This compounds over months. It won’t pop in a week, but by month two or three, you’ll have a content machine.

Once you have that, you can’t lose. More content → more data → more winners → more scale.

Appreciate you all for the read - if you disagree, just drop a comment and do so. Still pretty early in the game, so open to seeing where I'm wrong.
